props.raw: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.

props.raw:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools

Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

Programmes: B.Tech. CSE
Year: 3rd/4th year
Assumed background: Strong programming and software development fundamentals;
familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.

Lab required: Yes — hands-on coding and development activities

Available infrastructure: Student development machines, access to
AI coding tools/APIs, software development environments, and TA support.

Preferred components: Practical assignments, hands-on coding exercises,
project-based evaluation, and a final project.

Components to avoid: none

Rationale: Assessment should emphasize the ability to apply modern
AI-assisted development practices rather than primarily testing theory.

[NONE]
CRITICAL: The final exam must be scheduled in week 2, covering topics from week 14.

Advanced software-development course positioned around emerging AI-native development practices. It builds on programming and software engineering foundations while introducing agent-assisted development, modern tooling, specification-driven workflows, automated evaluation, and software-factory concepts.

props.title: Agent Orchestration Setup
props.exercise: Configure a local agent orchestration framework (such as LangGraph) on student development machines. Set up environment variables, configure API keys, and verify connectivity by executing a basic single-agent prompt template.

props.title: AI-Assisted Bug Fixing
props.exercise: Run a pre-configured coding agent on a provided Python repository to resolve simple bugs. Students must configure static analysis tools to ensure that the agent's output produces no warnings and passes all public tests.

props.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration
props.exercise: Implement a multi-agent system where a coder agent and a tester agent collaborate. The coder agent generates code to solve a programming task, while the tester agent executes tests and provides feedback iteratively.

props.title: Gherkin Feature Construction
props.exercise: Translate natural language user stories and requirements documents into Gherkin feature files for a specified use-case, ensuring complete coverage of all functional requirements.

props.title: Executable Spec Implementation
props.exercise: Implement step definitions in Python for the Gherkin feature files created in Week 4. Execute the specifications to validate system behavior and verify that all tests pass.

props.title: MCP Server Setup
props.exercise: Implement a basic server-side Model Context Protocol (MCP) connection handler. Define custom data schemas to expose local database schemas to an external agent.

props.title: Mid-Semester Catch-up and Review
props.exercise: Open lab session for catching up on previous labs, debugging MCP handlers, and preparing for mid-semester evaluations. No new content is introduced.

props.title: Secure Tool Integration
props.exercise: Integrate custom tools into an MCP server and implement secure execution of these tools using a Docker-based sandbox environment to prevent unauthorized system access.

props.title: Agent Loop Tracing
props.exercise: Trace the execution of an iterative coding agent loop using LangSmith. Analyze execution logs to map the agent's decision steps and identify state transitions.

props.title: Reliability and Failure Analysis
props.exercise: Analyze execution logs of 100 automated agent runs to identify, categorize, and document at least three distinct failure modes, providing supporting log evidence.

props.title: Workflow Debugging
props.exercise: Debug a failing multi-agent workflow by modifying prompt templates and tool schemas based on failure analysis, ensuring the workflow successfully completes the task.

props.title: Multi-Component Deployment
props.exercise: Deploy a multi-component AI-native application consisting of a frontend, an orchestrator, and multiple MCP tools using Docker Compose.

props.title: Workflow Evaluation & Justification
props.exercise: Conduct a structured evaluation of the deployed workflow, writing a design justification report that maps each design decision against stated system requirements.

Collaborative design of MCP custom schemas for a mock weather and calendar service on paper.
Mid-sem review session. Worked walkthrough of sample exam questions on requirements and MCP protocol design.
Interactive threat-modeling of tool execution, identifying potential security exploits in unsandboxed environments.
Worked trace-diagnosis of 3 failing agent runs using execution logs, identifying where the loop diverged.
Group analysis of reliability metrics and plotting failure distributions from a provided dataset of agent executions.
Mock presentation session where students defend their workflow design choices against peer evaluator questions.
Interactive architectural mapping of a multi-component AI application, identifying potential bottlenecks.
Peer evaluation and structured feedback on draft design justification documents using a provided rubric.
